Refute

/rih-FYOOT/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Refute means to prove a statement, claim, or argument wrong, especially with evidence.

Refute means to prove a statement, claim, or argument wrong, especially with evidence

Worked Example

Dr. Alvarez spent the whole winter gathering satellite measurements so she could <strong style="color:var(--accent);">refute</strong> the claim that the glacier had stopped shrinking.

Dr. Alvarez is collecting hard satellite evidence for the specific purpose of proving the claim false. Setting out to disprove a claim with evidence is precisely what it means to refute it.

How Refute Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

disprove

disprove: to show something is false; the plainest equivalent

rebut

rebut: to argue back against a claim, without necessarily defeating it

debunk

debunk: to expose a myth or exaggeration, usually in a lighter, popular register

Antonyms

confirm

confirm: to show something is true

uphold

uphold: to support or keep a decision or claim in force

How Strong Is It? — doubt → dispute → refute

doubt vs. refute

doubt vs. refute: To doubt a claim is only to suspect it privately, while to refute it is to prove it wrong.

dispute vs. refute

dispute vs. refute: To dispute a claim is to argue openly against it, but to refute it is to actually demolish it with evidence.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, against

Root — -fute

Root — -fute: to beat, to strike down (Latin futare)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (back) plus -fute (to beat or strike) literally builds 'to beat back': when you refute a claim, you strike it down with proof.

Use the root in a new word: irrefutable

Use the root in a new word: irrefutable: An argument so airtight that no one can prove it wrong is irrefutable, the same root wearing the prefix ir-, meaning 'not able to be refuted.'

Root Check

Word Choice

formal-academic

Refute means to disprove, not merely to reject; you cannot 'refute an invitation.' Its cousin 'rebut' means to argue back against a claim, while refuting goes further by actually proving the claim wrong.
